newsitem.title: GREECE: Guerrillas kill Greek shipowner Peratikos -police.
newsitem.headline: Guerrillas kill Greek shipowner Peratikos -police.

text.p: Suspected urban guerrillas shot dead Greek shipowner Constantine Peratikos on Wednesday in an ambush as he walked to his car, police said.

"We believe it is the work of a terrorist group, but until the ballistic tests are in we can't tell which one," a senior police officer told Reuters. Earlier police had said it was unclear whether the three gunmen were criminals or guerrillas.

The attack appeared similar to those staged by the November 17 and May 1 leftist groups. November 17 has killed 21 people but has been dormant since a bungled rocket attack on the U.S. embassy in January 1996.
Peratikos, 42, was ambushed by three gunmen who fled in a hijacked taxi. Hospital officials said he was dead before reaching Piraeus' Tzanio Hospital.
The Peratikos Group, owned by one of Greece's major shipping families, bought the troubled Elefsis Shipyards in the early 1990s, but the shipyards have since reverted to state hands.
